recognize_zh: 高倍 GMS 染色：綠色壞死背景中滿布黑灰色輪廓的圓形與卵圓形酵母型真菌，大小不一，部分有出芽，另有拉長的形態，說明乾酪樣肉芽腫是真菌感染所致。
features: Innumerable GMS-positive round to oval yeast forms with dark walls and paler centers
Variation in yeast size with occasional larger forms and narrow-based budding
Elongated/ovoid forms in parallel arrays, without clear septate hyphae
Organisms concentrated at the edge of green-counterstained necrosis
describe_en: High-power GMS stain shows innumerable silver-positive fungal organisms at the margin of green-counterstained necrosis. The organisms are predominantly round to oval yeast forms with dark walls, variable size and occasional narrow-based budding, admixed with elongated ovoid forms; well-formed septate hyphae are not seen. Definitive speciation is not possible from morphology alone at this resolution. Findings are consistent with fungal infection as the cause of the necrotizing splenic granulomas; correlation with culture, mucicarmine, antigen testing or molecular identification is recommended.

ddx.vs: Histoplasma yeasts are small (2–4 µm), uniform and typically intracellular within macrophages, whereas these vary in size.
Cryptococcus shows variable-size yeasts with narrow-based budding and a mucicarmine-positive capsule, which would confirm it.
Blastomyces yeasts are larger (8–15 µm) with thick double-contoured walls and broad-based budding.
Candida shows small budding yeasts together with pseudohyphae with constrictions, which the elongated forms here should be assessed for.
